correctness.rationale: Free cyclic descent takes the two summands to A^{-1} and M, with deg A=1 and M of exact order m: a trivialization of a power of the character line upstairs differs from the given trivialization by a constant unit. The first fiber coordinate is a section of the pullback of A^{-1}, with simple zero F. On F, t^m gives the scheme fiber mB at zero; at a nonzero s the simply transitive action on its roots gives E, mapping to B by q. Picard invariance and divisor localization then give Cl(X_m)=Pic(B)/<A> with unique degree-zero representatives. The maps to the ordinary local rings are surjections. If a representative N becomes principal locally, its pullback agrees with a principal divisor modulo F near the fiber. Restriction to the reduced fiber gives N=A^a at o or q^*N=L^a at x_s, and degree forces a=0 in either case. Trivializations on E identify ker(q^*) with the constant character group <M>. The cover over s≠0 is finite étale by freeness on the t-coordinate, so Gorenstein descent kills the canonical class there. The total-space determinant gives K_W=π^*(A⊗M^{-1}), so this class generates <M> modulo F, proving the reverse kernel inclusion. Surjectivity of the dual isogeny gives the indicated target, and the elliptic Picard groups contain nontorsion classes. The proof uses only the reduced fiber at o to detect classes; the scheme multiplicity assertion is about F→Z. There is no finite computation dependency.
residual_risks: The class-group assertions concern the specified closed points and ordinary algebraic local rings, not completions, strict henselizations, or a map between local rings at distinct points.
